title: Naturality and open restriction of the external evaluation transpose
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X,Y,P$ schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $a:P\to X$, $b:P\to Y$ scheme morphisms. Work on small representatives of their small etale sites in one module universe [def-weil-size-convention], in the ordinary unbounded constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Inverse image and derived tensor are [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-kun-derived-tensor]. For any scheme $T$ and $G,M\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, set
$$\mathsf H_T(G,M)=R\Gamma(T,R\mathcal Hom_A(G,M))\in D(A),$$
using [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the derived constant/sections adjunction [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]; write $\underline Q_T$ for constant realization [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. For every $Q\in D(A)$ there is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(Q,\mathsf H_T(G,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T,A)}(\underline Q_T\otimes_A^LG,M).$$
It sends the identity of $\mathsf H_T(G,M)$ to evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_{G,M}$.

For arbitrary $E,K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $H,L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put $C=\mathsf H_X(E,K)$, $D=\mathsf H_Y(H,L)$, $G=a^{-1}E\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}H$ and $F=a^{-1}K\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}L$. The transpose of
$$\underline{C\otimes_A^LD}_P\otimes_A^LG\xrightarrow{\chi}(a^{-1}\underline C_X\otimes_A^La^{-1}E)\otimes_A^L(b^{-1}\underline D_Y\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}H)\xrightarrow{a^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_{E,K}\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}\mathrm{ev}_{H,L}}F$$
is a well-defined morphism $\beta_{E,H}:C\otimes_A^LD\to\mathsf H_P(G,F)$. Here $\chi$ uses the canonical constant-pullback and strong monoidal comparisons and the symmetry interchanging $\underline D$ with $a^{-1}E$, whose cochain sign is $(-1)^{|z||e|}$. The morphisms $\beta$ are contravariantly natural in $E,H$ and covariantly natural in $K,L$. For an open immersion $j:X'\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], put $P'=P\times_X X'$, $k:P'\to P$, $a':P'\to X'$ and $b'=bk$. Restriction of global derived morphisms induces maps on each $\mathsf H$; the square from $\beta_{E,H}$ to $\beta_{j^{-1}E,H}$ with these restriction maps commutes under $k^{-1}G\cong a'^{-1}j^{-1}E\otimes_A^Lb'^{-1}H$ and $k^{-1}F\cong a'^{-1}j^{-1}K\otimes_A^Lb'^{-1}L$. The analogous assertion holds for restriction of $Y$. No boundedness or flatness hypothesis is imposed.
